transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
I came because… I’ve been hearing voices. Like someone’s right there in my studio, clear, saying my name… saying my work is being judged. But nobody’s there. It’s quiet.
How long have you been hearing these voices?
About… nine months, I think. The voices, and that feeling like my work’s being watched… it’s been going on since around then.
Do the voices ever tell you to do something?
Not really… it’s more like they say my name, and talk like my work is being judged. Like someone’s right there, but nobody is.
Do you hear one voice or multiple voices?

It’s… hard to say. Mostly it feels like one voice, clear, like somebody’s standing right there in the studio saying my name. Sometimes it’s like there’s more than one, talking about my work being judged.
Are the voices ever critical of you or your work?
Yeah… sometimes. It sounds like they’re saying my work is being judged. Like they’re right there in the room with me, even when it’s quiet and nobody’s there.
Are the voices you hear inside your head or outside of it?
Outside… it sounds like somebody’s right there in my little studio, saying my name. Not like just thoughts in my head.
Have these voices and feelings of being judged affected your daily life or ability to work?

Yeah… it has. I don’t really like saying it, but my aide job got shaky. I missed some shifts, and I was mixing up care notes, not keeping the visits straight like I used to.

And I stopped going to my walking club and those art talks at the library. Mostly I’ve just been home by myself.
Do you ever find it hard to express your thoughts or have trouble keeping your conversations organized and on track?
I don’t know… maybe sometimes I lose my place. But I’m not sure if it’s that, or just me getting tired. I try to keep it short so I don’t get mixed up.
Do you believe that your work is actually being judged or watched by someone, even when you're alone?

Yeah… I do. I know people say it doesn’t add up, but it feels real.

Like the other home-care agency, and some people from the library… I thought they were looking at my paintings and even my client papers. Like they were trying to take some chance that was supposed to be mine. Even when I’m by myself, I still feel like they’re watching.
Do you often find yourself having trouble understanding what people are saying to you, or do you have difficulty making yourself understood by others?

I’m not really sure. I mean… sometimes I ask people to repeat themselves, but I don’t know if that’s what you mean.

I don’t think I have a big problem making people understand me. I just try not to say too much.
Do you often feel like your thoughts are disjointed or hard to put into words?
I don’t know… not often, I guess. Sometimes I can’t find the right words, but I don’t really think about it that way. I just keep it short.
Do you often feel like you're having trouble putting your thoughts together when you're talking to someone?
I don’t really know. Maybe sometimes I lose what I was trying to say, but… I wouldn’t say it happens a lot. I usually just stop talking if it feels messy.
Do you often feel like your thoughts are disconnected from each other?

Yeah… sometimes it’s like they jump around too fast. I’ll be thinking about one thing, like a client’s medicine, and then it’s rent, then some painting name, then something I heard in a song. It gets hard to slow it down enough to make sense.
Do you feel like your thoughts are disorganized or hard to follow when you're thinking to yourself?

Yeah… inside my own head it can be hard to follow. It runs too fast sometimes—like medicine for a client, then rent, then some painting name, then a song meaning something. I don’t really… slow it down easy.
Have you noticed any changes in your behavior or actions that seem unusual or unpredictable to you or others?

I guess… yeah, some things. Like on visits, I’ve stopped doing what I was there for and started lining up gloves or pill cups, little scraps from crochet, making patterns. Or I’ll just stand in a hallway staring, like I’m waiting for something. People notice. I don’t always know why I’m doing it.
Can you tell me more about what you mean by lining up gloves or pill cups and making patterns during your visits?

It’s… hard to explain. I’ll be at a client’s place and I’m supposed to be doing something, but then I’ll start putting the gloves or pill cups in rows, or making little patterns with scraps from crochet. Sometimes I just end up standing in the hallway, staring, like I’m waiting for… some kind of signal or something. I don’t always realize how long I’m doing it.
Have you noticed doing things in a repetitive or ritualistic way that doesn't seem to have a purpose?

Yeah… I guess that’s what it is. Like I said, I’ll stop what I’m supposed to be doing and start lining up gloves or pill cups, little crochet scraps… making them into patterns. Or I just stand there in the hallway staring, like I’m waiting for something. It doesn’t really have a reason, not that I can explain.
Have these voices and feelings of being watched been constant over the nine months, or have they come and gone?
They’ve… mostly been there. Not every second, but it hasn’t really gone away. The voices and that feeling about work being watched have been happening for about nine months now.
Do you often feel like your thoughts are not making sense to you or to others?

Yeah… sometimes. It’s like my thoughts go too fast. I’ll be thinking about a client’s medicine, then rent, then some painting title, then a song feels like it has some message in it. It jumps around, and I can’t slow it down enough to make sense.
Have you ever had a period of time where your symptoms, such as the voices and feelings of being watched, were much worse for a short time, and then got better?
Not really short, no. It’s been… kind of steady. The voices and that fear about work being watched have been going on about nine months now.
